gap_reasons: The delivered proofs establish protocol-uniform oracle-submodel domination and a matching original-model minimax ATE limit, including measurable reconstruction and estimation of the unknown control mean. Maximality fixes the control mean, and the asymptotics cover the specified rare-treatment/privacy boundary uniformly on compact positive public-parameter sets; they do not establish global unknown-control equivalence or a broader privacy frontier, and the framing preserves those distinctions without a stale overclaim. The inspected [Nam–Park–Lee theorem](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.02319v1) characterizes finite-channel Blackwell maximality, while [Shvets’s theorem](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.10073v1) concerns neighboring shuffled-data experiments, leaving the sequential population comparison distinct from those predecessors. The general value characterization and convergent certificates are delivered, but exhaustive rational enumeration has no demonstrated practical implementation, and the sole executed numerical benchmark lies inside the endpoint-prior sufficient region. The restricted boundary regime and missing general-intensity computational evidence constrain the projected leading-journal score and the claimed usefulness for pilot planning. proof_attempt_summary: Derived a protocol-uniform measurable simulator on countably generated release spaces, matched the original unknown-control ATE minimax limit, and supplied canonical decision certificates. The mathematical referee passed with all eight citations verified, but novelty achieved subfield (score ceiling 7.2) below the field floor; the main validity consult confirmed that the two decision-referee ballast findings are non-load-bearing redundancy. No Lean formalization was attempted; preserve the informal derivation for re-raise, with scope and computational limitations disclosed.
tldr: A randomized binary pilot with treatment probability \(\lambda/n\) has a finite-information rare arm. At full-record local privacy budget \(\log(n/\rho)\), the independent Poisson pair with intensities \(\rho+\lambda(1-\mu_1)\) and \(\rho+\lambda\mu_1\) asymptotically dominates every sequential transcript in each fixed-control oracle submodel. The comparison covers nonempty measurable release spaces with countably generated sigma fields. Four-category randomized response retains the rare experiment and estimates the unknown control mean; one certified transcript-only procedure attains the original-model all-protocol minimax ATE MSE, uniformly on compact positive public-parameter sets. The limiting value has an exact least-favorable-prior/posterior-mean characterization and finite evaluable certificates at any supplied tolerance. A sufficient small-intensity region also admits the explicit endpoint posterior rule.
gap: Regular-model local privacy theory describes Gaussian efficiency at fixed models and budgets. Finite-channel Blackwell geometry and shuffled neighboring-dataset Poisson limits do not determine one greatest sequential population experiment when \(np_n=\lambda\).
fill: The project compares all admissible transcripts with the Poisson pair, transfers bounded squared loss in an oracle submodel, and constructs a transcript-only release and certified decision rule attaining the same original-model risk uniformly.
